checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that global shape checkpoints (pear-shape, ostiole) are untestable or not present due to the slicing of the fruit. This is a logical adaptation to the image content. The verdicts for the internal structure (seeds, pulp, texture) are accurate and supported by visual evidence. The Router was not too lenient; it appropriately marked 'is_present: false' for features that simply cannot be seen in a cross-section.
artifact_review: The Router identified minor texture anomalies (severity 1.5) and boundary softness (severity 1.0). The Perceptual Quality Auditor found no graphics-level distortions (noise/compression), which supports the high quality of the generation. The Topology Boundary Auditor's mask (0.97 confidence) confirms strong object coherence. However, looking closely at the central fig's interior, the seed distribution is extremely dense and slightly 'muddy' in the very center, which is a common AI artifact in macro food shots where fine detail collapses into noise. The Router's severity rating of 1.5 is appropriate—it's noticeable but doesn't break the illusion. I agree with the Router's assessment that these are minor issues.
alignment_reasoning: The Fine-Grained Classifier strongly confirms the class 'fig' (logit 8.3 vs 1.97 for next best). All testable internal checkpoints (seeds, pulp color, jam-like texture, thin skin) are fully present and visually accurate. The image perfectly captures the botanical reality of a sliced fig. Un-testable external checkpoints were correctly ignored.
artifact_reasoning: No catastrophic structural failures. Minor texture clumping in the central seed mass (Router severity 1.5) and slight edge softness on one slice (Router severity 1.0) are the only noted issues. These are consistent with macro photography depth-of-field or minor synthesis noise, not major AI artifacts. The high mask confidence and lack of perceptual distortion support a high artifact score.
